learn.title: Factors that affect cost, and cost management
objectives: Name the main factors that change what you pay in Azure.
Spot hidden costs such as orphaned resources, egress and Marketplace charges.
Explain what Microsoft Cost Management does: cost analysis, budgets, alerts, forecasts and exports.
Choose the right scope for viewing and controlling costs.
Know what budgets and alerts can and can't do.
concepts: Resource type and size
Each service is priced by its own meters (hours, GB, transactions). Bigger sizes, premium tiers and extra features cost more.
Consumption
You pay for what runs and what's stored. Usage up means cost up, and the reverse.
Maintenance and orphaned resources
Deleting a VM can leave behind disks, public IPs, snapshots and NICs that keep billing. Clean them up.
Geography
Prices vary between regions because of local power, tax and labour costs.
Network traffic
Inbound data is free. Outbound (egress) and some inter-region traffic is charged, and rates vary by bandwidth zone.
Subscription type
Free, pay-as-you-go, Dev/Test, Enterprise Agreement and other offers have different rates, credits and spending limits.
Azure Marketplace
Third-party products can add their own charges on top of the Azure infrastructure they run on.
Microsoft Cost Management
Built-in tools to analyse, monitor, forecast and optimise Azure spending.
Budgets
Spending thresholds over a period (month, quarter or year) that trigger alerts when actual or forecast cost crosses them.
Cost alerts
Budget alerts, credit alerts (Azure Prepayment) and department spending quota alerts (Enterprise Agreement), plus anomaly alerts.
comparisons: A budget alerts you; it doesn't stop resources by itself. A spending limit (free and credit-based offers) disables resources when the credit runs out.
Actual cost shows purchases when they're billed. Amortized cost spreads a reservation purchase across its term.
Cost analysis shows where money went. Advisor recommends how to spend less.
More copies and regions cost more: LRS is cheapest, then ZRS, GRS and GZRS.
traps: Budgets don't automatically stop or delete resources. They notify, and can trigger action groups you set up.
Deleting a VM doesn't automatically delete its disks or public IP.
Inbound data transfer is free; outbound isn't.
The same VM size can cost different amounts in different regions.
Cost Management data isn't real-time; it can take hours to appear.
revision: Cost factors: resource type, consumption, maintenance, geography, network traffic, subscription type, Marketplace.
Cost Management = cost analysis, budgets, alerts, forecasts, exports, recommendations.
Scopes: billing account, management group, subscription, resource group.
Budgets alert on actual or forecast cost and reset monthly, quarterly or annually.
Exports send cost data on a schedule to a storage account.
Orphaned disks and IPs are a common source of surprise charges.
